note: Generated by tools/fetch-hallplan.mjs from the `hallen` array on the hall-plan page (SOURCE below) — the outline Koelnmesse draws the whole site from before you pick a hall. A DIAGRAM, NOT A PLAN: the rings are on a 5-unit grid and every hall is fitted to its slot on the official artwork rather than drawn to scale, so neighbouring halls come out at different scales (hall 6 at about 1.5 m per unit across, hall 4 at 1.6, and 1.4 against 2.1 down) and no single scale converts this file to metres. What it is right about is the arrangement: which hall is where, which wall faces the Boulevard, and what joins what — which is the whole job of an overview. A hall's own geometry is in its hall-<id>.json, in true metres. FRAME: x runs west to east and y north to south, the same way round as a hall file, with 0,0 at the north-west corner of everything drawn; `size` is the extent. FEATURES: kind is hall, concourse (the Boulevard and the Piazza), passage (every Durchgang and Passage between two halls, and the entrance halls), outdoor (the open-air areas) or building (the Confex and the Congress-Centrum wings). id is Koelnmesse's own code, which for a hall is its number. `levels` names the hall levels this guide draws, so the overview knows which plates open into a map and which are there for orientation only; `area` is that hall's area, the same key as in index.json. `place` is a name worth putting on the diagram, as an i18n key the client resolves (map.place.*) — ours, because the source labels none of these. ENTRANCES: id and a point, one per gate. They are the dots on the site artwork the page lays over these outlines, whose frame is this one shifted 134 units — a dot is a coordinate, so we take the points and none of the drawing, and the names are the client's, from map.gate.*. Four of them, not the six the artwork marks: that artwork is Koelnmesse's traffic guide for the grounds and marks every way in the buildings have, while gamescom opens Nord, Ost, Sued and West. See CAMPUS_ENTRANCES in the tool. Re-running this tool rewrites the file; a correction belongs in the tool, not here.
